title: Harness: Cloth, Armour and Gear Movement Sound Effects
shortText: 152 foley SFX: cloth, cloak, leather, mail, plate and a pack moving at 4 gaits, walk loops, moves. WAV + OGG.
html:
What your character's clothes, armour and kit do when they move, as a layer on top of your footsteps

152 foley sound effects for six garments: cloth, heavy cloak, leather, mail, plate, adventurer's kit. Every garment at four gaits (walk, run, sneak, land), walk loops that stack into outfits, six body moves, putting each garment on and taking it off, buckles and straps and pouches, and idle loops.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No credit required. No revenue limit, no unit cap, no second licence to buy later if your game does well. Use it in as many projects as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell the sounds themselves as sounds. The full plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy paste credit line if you want one.

Everything is synthesised from code. No recordings, no sample libraries, no third party clips, so there is no upstream licence behind this one and nobody can content ID claim these sounds against your project.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 19 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. One walk step in all six garments, mail at all four gaits, two walk loops to stack, a dodge roll in cloth, mail and plate, plate put on and taken off, and a little handling.

What is in it

  • Step layer: Cloth (12)
  • Step layer: Heavy cloak (12)
  • Step layer: Leather (12)
  • Step layer: Mail (12)
  • Step layer: Plate (12)
  • Step layer: Adventurer's kit (12)
  • Walk loops (6)
  • Body moves (36)
  • Put on and take off (12)
  • Handling (20)
  • Idle loops (6)

The layer that goes on top of a footstep

Most footstep packs give you the foot. This is the rest of the body: a mail shirt jingling as the heel lands, a cloak's hem snapping, leather creaking, plates clanking at the joints, a pack bouncing with its tin cup. The gait ids are the ones a footstep system already uses (walk, run, sneak, land), so the same call that plays the footstep plays the body layer. Every walk, run and land file has its jolt in its first 20 ms, where a footstep's heel is (measured on all 54).

Each garment at each gait is its own sound: 36 gait pairs and 60 garment pairs measured apart on the shipped files, 0 too close. Three takes per cell, so nothing repeats step after step.

Walk loops that stack into outfits

6 walk loops, one per garment, 4 seconds, 120 steps a minute, every step on the same grid as the walk loops in our footstep pack Footfall (measured against its files: the furthest step 8.12 ms off the heel). They share one length and one step grid, so they stack: a knight is cloth, then mail, then plate; a ranger is a cloak, leather and a pack; a sellsword is leather with mail over it. 8 stacks re-summed from the shipped files, each wrapping cleanly.

Moves, and putting it on

Turn, jump, crouch, rise, a dodge roll and a fall, in every garment. Putting each one on uses the fastening it really has: laces, a cloak brooch, buckles, a mail shirt's belt, three plate straps, a pack's two straps and its chest buckle; taking it off ends with it dropped on the floor. 216 pairs measured apart across those two grids. Plus buckles, straps, pouches, a pack shouldered and set down and rummaged in, a gauntlet, a visor, a sword belt and a cloak swirl, and an idle loop per garment for a character who stands and waits.

Already own our other packs?

Where this pack fills a role one of 9 of our other packs already fills (a cloth rustle, a crouch, a body falling, a strap pulled tight, a dodge), the two were measured against each other from both packs' files: 25 shared roles, every one a different sound.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, dry (no reverb, so your own reverb places it), with a manifest by slot.
  • 12 seamless loops with sample accurate loop points in the WAV and the OGG.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.02 dB.
  • pack_proof.json ships with the pack: 1391 checks, 0 failed.
  • No footsteps, no weapons swung, no hits on armour, no voices or breathing. It is the layer between those.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds, not recordings of real armour. The measurements above are signal measurements, not a claim that it sounds good. That is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Footfall, the footsteps this layer sits on: twelve surfaces, four gaits, three weights, walk loops on the same grid.
  • Wade, the wet half: footsteps and movement in water, mud and puddles.
  • Steel and Bone, the hits: eight weapons and a fist on plate, shields, mail, leather, flesh and stone.
